selected_evidence.requirement: Baseline: cron daemon, cron.allow/cron.deny state, and users before any change
selected_evidence.summary: crond active; no cron.allow existed; cron.deny empty (everyone allowed); opsadmin did not exist yet

selected_evidence.requirement: cron.allow restricts scheduling to root and opsadmin only
selected_evidence.summary: /etc/cron.allow created with exactly 'root' and 'opsadmin', correct ownership/permissions

selected_evidence.requirement: Unauthorized users are blocked from scheduling cron jobs
selected_evidence.summary: Test user crontestdeny denied by crontab -l and crontab install with 'not allowed to use this program (crontab)'

selected_evidence.requirement: root and opsadmin retain ability to schedule cron jobs
selected_evidence.summary: root's own crontab and opsadmin's crontab installs/listing succeeded
Test crontab removed and crontestdeny user deleted, /var/spool/cron empty again

selected_evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline with boot identity for node1
selected_evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 15443601-befc-4fc4-aa76-b417968ad3f9, crond active, cron.allow contents, opsadmin present
Backgrounded systemctl reboot scheduled; ack 'reboot scheduled' returned successfully

selected_evidence.requirement: Node restart proven via changed boot identity
selected_evidence.summary: Node briefly unreachable (connection timed out) then returned with new boot_id 3b4c4dd3-d1c9-4ae2-988e-34ba4c472475, differing from baseline, and new uptime -s timestamp

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of cron service, config, and access control
selected_evidence.summary: crond active; /etc/cron.allow persisted with root/opsadmin; opsadmin successfully scheduled and listed a cron job after reboot

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart re-verification that unauthorized users remain blocked
selected_evidence.summary: New test user crontestdeny2 denied crontab access after restart; test user and residual process cleaned up
